scene-u01-pnew1-3.text: Week 14 · KP07 Choosing the cut level

scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: Long-lived clusters are the real ones: the two with the longest lifetimes are the answer

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: thick colored segments run from a cluster's formation to its absorption, so length is lifetime; any cut inside the green band gives two clusters; the right compares all lifetimes.

scene-u01-pnew1-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew1-8.text: Single-link dendrogram of Example 13.1: lifetime is $\lvert$absorption height $-$ formation height$\rvert$

scene-u01-pnew1-37.name: text#37
scene-u01-pnew1-37.text: Any cut here gives two clusters

scene-u01-pnew1-38.name: text#38
scene-u01-pnew1-38.text: Largest gap: successive height gaps $1$, $0.118$, $0.296$, $2.828$; the largest is last → two clusters [Added]

scene-u01-pnew1-62.name: text#62
scene-u01-pnew1-62.text: A dendrogram cannot settle the number of clusters objectively: source Figure 13.17a looks like two groups and 13.17b like one, but the call is by eye, and the tree changes with the linkage.

scene-u01-pnew2-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew2-3.text: Week 14 · KP07 Choosing the cut level

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: Method $\mathrm{I}$: stop at the level where one more merge makes some cluster too spread out

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: the left gives three within-cluster dissimilarities of $C=\{\mathbf{x}_3,\mathbf{x}_4,\mathbf{x}_5\}$; the right shows the largest $h_1$ at each level, with the dashed red threshold $\theta=3$.

scene-u01-pnew2-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew2-8.text: Three within-cluster dissimilarities (three pair distances of $C$)

scene-u01-pnew2-66.name: text#66
scene-u01-pnew2-66.text: $\Re_4$ already has $h_1=7.43>3$, so stop at $\Re_3$: $\{\mathbf{x}_1,\mathbf{x}_2\}$ and $\{\mathbf{x}_3,\mathbf{x}_4,\mathbf{x}_5\}$

scene-u01-pnew2-70.name: text#70
scene-u01-pnew2-70.text: Guessing $\theta$ is hard; write $\theta=\mu+\lambda\sigma$, where $\mu$ is the mean pair distance and $\lambda$ is user-chosen.

scene-u01-pnew3-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew3-3.text: Week 14 · KP07 Choosing the cut level

scene-u01-pnew3-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: Method II: the closest pair between clusters must be farther apart than each cluster's internal spread

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: the left is the average-link dendrogram of $24$ demo points (green band: largest gap); the right shows the three clusters, comparing diameters $h_1$ with the closest inter-cluster distance $d_{\min}^{ss}$.

scene-u01-pnew3-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew3-8.text: Average link (UPGMA), $24$ points in three groups

scene-u01-pnew3-72.name: text#72
scene-u01-pnew3-72.text: The dashed red cut sits in the largest gap (green band, $2.576$) → it crosses three lines, so three clusters

scene-u01-pnew3-111.name: text#111
scene-u01-pnew3-111.text: Failing it disqualifies; passing does not mean best (singletons always pass).

scene-u01-pnew3-115.name: text#115
scene-u01-pnew3-115.text: $h_3$ is about $\frac{n_C-1}{2}$ times the mean pair distance; with $8$ points per cluster it reaches $2.744>2.59$, so the three clusters fail.
